messages:
josh (support): customer ClearPath opened ticket summarizing two asks: they want streaming completions with function/tool-calling so our agent can start invoking long-running ops before the full response finishes. ticket: <https://support.redwood.ai/t/3421>

nish (sales): ClearPath is our onboarding pilot for Q2. if we can promise partial function invocation + structured JSON frames they will commit to Dedicated seats. this is revenue-impacting. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sara (product): thanks — we need to triage. can we get a quick scope proposal: what is the minimal ship (MVP) vs stretch? also list acceptance criteria and launch blockers.

kevin (eng-runtime): quick gut: MVP = token-streaming + ability to emit a function call frame early (with a stable schema) + explicit finalization event. stretch = resumable/k-v-cached partial invocations and client-side ack/retry. runtime risks: partial tool calls need atomic commit semantics on retries. also need to ensure prefix cache behavior doesn't break streaming order.

maya (devex): SDK impact: we'll need new stream event types and client helpers to assemble partial function payloads and validate schema client-side. docs + examples + TS/py SDK changes. estimate: 2 weeks for SDK/Docs once runtime API is stable.

nish (sales): is there a cheaper interim we can offer ClearPath? like non-resumable partial calls but with explicit 'early-invoke' flag? they just need low-latency start to background jobs.

sara (product): propose: MVP = "early-invoke" streaming frame + structured JSON frames for arguments + non-resumable. Canary with ClearPath on Dedicated. Acceptance criteria: 1) stream frames support `type: token` / `type: fn_call_start` / `type: fn_call_arg_chunk` / `type: fn_call_end` 2) a clear SDK assembly helper for fn args 3) documented fallback: full non-stream fncall 4) performance: 95p first-token < 150ms on dedicated profile 5) no correctness regressions on existing chat/completions.

kevin (eng-runtime): sounds doable but need to flag two blockers: (A) kernel scheduling & batcher needs a hook to emit fn_call_start as soon as condition met, (B) storage for partial fn args before we atomically commit them on fn_call_end. estimate: 3-4 engineer-weeks if we can re-use existing streaming infra.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist created -> https://go.redwood.ai/tasks/stream-fncall-1957772468 (auto)

josh (support): question from ClearPath: "if fn args are large (10s of KB), will streaming still send arg chunks reliably? any token loss risk?"

kevin (eng-runtime): chunking is fine but we need explicit sequence numbers in frames and a checksum on fn_call_end to validate integrity. add that to acceptance criteria.

sara (product): updated acceptance: add sequence numbers + checksum for fn args. also add rollout criteria: must pass a ClearPath pilot for 2 weeks with no data-loss incidents and SDK integration sample.

maya (devex): I'll draft SDK PR template and sample app (Next.js agent + background job) to show how to assemble streamed fn args and trigger local simulate/replay.

nish (sales): if engineering can commit to the MVP in the next quarter we will move ClearPath contract up to signature. pushing for P1. :rocket:

kevin (eng-runtime): reality check: P1 timeline if we re-prioritize current sprint (pull 1 engineer from runtime infra). otherwise P2. I'll update the estimate in the ticket.

sara (product): decision: tentative P1, but final priority after eng head sign-off. action items: kevin to post an eng plan + risk list by EOD, maya to add SDK checklist, josh to confirm ClearPath pilot acceptance criteria in the ticket, and I'll draft the launch checklist (SLOs, docs, canary plan).

nish (sales): thanks team. i'll let ClearPath know we're initiating scoping. :eyes:

kevin (eng-runtime): plan posted: https://go.redwood.ai/epics/1957772468-plan — includes sequence numbers, checksum, and storage design. will follow up with timeline.
